Complete Empirical Research Plan

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Chosen strategy: Multi-period, multi-group Difference-in-Differences (DID) augmented with an event-study and implemented as a “triple-difference” (DDD) specification.

Why appropriate  
• The Clean Air Act created discrete, annually updated attainment / non-attainment classifications that vary across counties, years, and pollutants.  
• Only plants in industries that emit the pollutant are targeted. This naturally supplies two untreated baselines: (i) polluting plants in attainment counties and (ii) non-polluting plants in either county type.  
• The plant panel allows us to difference out time-invariant plant characteristics and to absorb rich county-year and industry-year shocks.  
• The staggered adoption of non-attainment status suggests supplementing DID with an event-study to test for pre-trends and dynamic effects.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
T_ictp = 1 if plant i in county c during census year t is in an industry that emits pollutant p AND county c is in non-attainment for pollutant p in year t (0 otherwise).  
Because the four pollutants matter, we will construct four pollutant-specific dummies and aggregate them into one indicator or intensity measure:

Treat_i c t  =  Σ_p  T_ictp    (range 0–4)  
Main specification uses a binary Treated = 1{Σ_p ≥ 1}.

Control groups  
Primary counterfactual = polluting plants in attainment counties.  
Additional controls (for DDD) = non-polluting plants in all counties.  
Thus the main estimating sample is all manufacturing plants; identification comes from the interaction of (Polluting × Non-attainment × Post).

Treatment timing  
County-pollutant moves from attainment to non-attainment the first year it exceeds the NAAQS. We assign the *first* non-attainment year between two Censuses to the subsequent Census observation. “Post” therefore equals 1 in every census after the county first becomes non-attainment for that pollutant.

No running variable / cutoff is required; this is not an RDD.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends: In the absence of the regulation, outcomes in treated and control groups would have evolved in parallel.  
Plausibility: contemporaneous macro shocks are absorbed by industry-year and county-year fixed effects; yet remaining concern about differential pre-trends motivates an event-study test.

A2. Stable Composition / No selective migration conditional on fixed effects: Plants do not sort endogenously across counties in reaction to anticipated status changes in a way that is correlated with outcomes.  
Plausibility: Moving an existing plant is costly, but firms could site new plants strategically. We will tackle this by (i) plant fixed effects (existing plants), (ii) estimating separately on new entrants vs incumbents, and (iii) including county×year FEs to soak up local investment climate.

A3. Exogenous timing of non-attainment status conditional on county×year trends: Counties cross the NAAQS threshold because of pollution realizations rather than strategic economic considerations. The EPA rule uses ambient readings independent of measured employment, etc., supporting the assumption.

A4. No spillovers between counties: Emissions and economic activity in a non-attainment county do not systematically affect neighboring attainment counties’ outcomes. Border-county robustness tests will gauge the importance of this.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential pre-trends / anticipation  
• Event-study coefficients for leads of treatment will be inspected.  
• If significant pre-trends appear, restrict sample to within-state, within-air-quality monitor pairs that show parallel pre-trends; or add county-specific linear time trends.

T2. Plant entry/exit driven by regulation (composition bias)  
• Estimate effects on (i) incumbent plants, (ii) net entry separately using a count model at county-industry level.  
• Weight regressions by 1967 plant employment to keep initial composition constant.  
• Use Inverse Probability Weights for survival if necessary.

T3. Measurement error in attainment coding (especially early years)  
• Cross-validate CFR status with monitor-based Quick Look data; create “certain non-attainment” indicator (only coded 1 when both sources agree).  
• Show robustness to dropping counties with uncertain status or that flip repeatedly.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
# --------------------------------------------------
# 0. Libraries
# --------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)     # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)         # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(ggplot2)        # plotting event study

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge data
# --------------------------------------------------
plants   <- fread("plants_cm_1967_1987.csv")   # plant-level census data
attain   <- fread("county_attainment_1967_1987.csv")  # county-year-pollutant

# Merge pollutant info into plants
# Assume plants has vars: plant_id, year, county_fips, sic4
# EPA lookup table: sic4 -> emits_CO, emits_O3, emits_SO2, emits_TSP
sic_poll <- fread("industry_emitter_flags.csv")

plants <- merge(plants, sic_poll, by = "sic4", all.x = TRUE)

# Replace NA with 0 for emitter flags
for(v in c("emits_CO","emits_O3","emits_SO2","emits_TSP")) 
  plants[is.na(get(v)), (v) := 0]

# Expand attainment to census years
attain_census <- attain[year %in% seq(1967,1987,5)]

plants <- merge(plants,
                attain_census,
                by = c("county_fips","year"),
                all.x = TRUE)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Treatment indicators
# --------------------------------------------------
# Pollutant-specific treated flags
for(p in c("CO","O3","SO2","TSP")){
  plants[ , paste0("treat_",p) := get(paste0("nonattain_",p)) * get(paste0("emits_",p))]
}

# Any pollutant
plants[ , treated := (treat_CO + treat_O3 + treat_SO2 + treat_TSP) >= 1 ]

# Pre/Post relative to first nonattainment for main pollutant of plant
# Example for TSP
setorder(attain, county_fips, year)
attain[ , first_nonattain_TSP := min(year[nonattain_TSP==1]), by = county_fips]
plants <- merge(plants, 
                attain[,.(county_fips, year, first_nonattain_TSP)],
                by = c("county_fips","year"))
plants[ , post_TSP := (year >= first_nonattain_TSP) ]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main specification
# --------------------------------------------------
# Outcome: ln employment (analogous for capital, output)
plants[ , ln_emp := log(employment)]

spec_main <- feols(ln_emp ~ treated | plant_id + county_fips^year + sic4^year,
                   data = plants,
                   cluster = ~county_fips)

summary(spec_main)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Event study
# --------------------------------------------------
# Years relative to first non-attainment (TSP example)
plants[ , rel_year := year - first_nonattain_TSP ]
plants <- plants[rel_year >= -10 & rel_year <= 10]   # trim extremes

# Build dummies
for(j in -10:10) plants[ , paste0("D",j) := as.integer(rel_year==j)]

fml_event <- as.formula(
  paste0("ln_emp ~ ", 
         paste(paste0("D", -5:-1), collapse="+"), " + ",   # leads
         paste(paste0("D",0:5), collapse="+"),            # lags incl 0
         " | plant_id + county_fips^year + sic4^year")
)

event <- feols(fml_event, data = plants, cluster = ~county_fips)
iplot(event, ref.line = 0)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness: county-specific linear trends
# --------------------------------------------------
plants[ , trend := year]
spec_trend <- feols(ln_emp ~ treated | plant_id + county_fips^trend + sic4^year,
                    data = plants, cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(spec_trend)
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Economic logic: Regulatory compliance raises marginal cost of production and new capital installation, especially for pollution-intensive industries. Hence:

• Employment: negative 3–5 % per five-year census in treated plants.  
• Capital stock: ambiguous—stringent “offset” rules may deter new investment (−5 %) but may also spur abatement capital (+). On net I expect a small negative.  
• Shipments / output: −2 % to −4 %.  
Magnitude loosely calibrated from compliance cost studies suggesting ~2 % of value added for regulated plants; elasticity of factor demand ≈ 0.6–0.8.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
-------------------------------------------------
C1: Pre-treatment parallel trends confirmed in event study ........ 0.8  
C2: No anticipation / timing exogenous ............................. 0.7  
C3: No spillovers across units ..................................... 0.6  
C4: Stable unit composition (no selective migration) ............... 0.6  
C5: Correct functional form / no time-varying treatment intensity .. 0.8  

(1 = clearly satisfied → 0.8; borderline → 0.6)

Overall, while credible, the design hinges on verifiable pre-trends and the absence of large spillovers; robustness checks and alternative samples are essential.
